⭐ the fixed engine->track-file entry, called once from engine_init. It arrives WITH the track data (the unpack swap deposits the track file over $5300-$5A25), so it is not a patch site. SILVER: 60 EA EA = RTS/NOP/NOP, a deliberate no-op for the circuit with no hook code. BRANDS: 4C 00 57 = JMP $5700. One call, one target — a far cleaner seam for the port than the five patch sites. ⭐⭐ IN THIS PORT IT IS CORRECTLY A NO-OP FOR EVERY CIRCUIT, and that is not the same as baking Silverstone's RTS by accident: on an expansion circuit $5A22 holds JMP $5700 = ModifyGameCode, whose whole job is to patch the engine, and the port applies that patcher's OUTPUT as data at selection time (tools/track_patch.py replays it; `make track-patch VERIFY=1` cross-checks the replay against a real BBC). Running it here would patch an already-patched image. The guarantee that the replay covered whatever is there is a GENERATION-time one: the replay's interpreter raises on any opcode outside its twelve-form vocabulary. src/platform/track.h, docs/phases.md §5.

the ONLY routine that programs the hardware: 6845 CRTC ($FE00/$FE01), Video ULA palette ($FE21), System VIA T1/ACR/IFR/IER, User VIA T1/ACR/IER. 54 instructions, one caller. This is the platform boundary.

⭐ THE RASTER-BAND PALETTE/MODE SCHEDULE, claimed via IRQ1V — and it DRAWS NOTHING (measured 2026-08-17; it was called 'the 50 Hz game body' until then, and that misnomer is why the row was carried as untouchable engine work). Driven by a USER VIA T1 timeout (LDA $FE6D / AND #$40), NOT System VIA vsync. One PAL field is five interrupts; each arm repaints the ULA mode + palette for the band about to be scanned and reloads the T1 latch with that band's duration — the raster split a BBC has to do on the CPU for want of a copper. Dispatches on irq_band_state; chains to saved_irq1v when the interrupt is not its own. The only game work in the whole cycle is the JSR body_tick_xor_anim ($52A4) in band 4: 206-233 us of a 6113 us field, i.e. 4%.

⭐⭐ [DERIVED] THE 3D VIEWPORT RASTERISER — the biggest main-loop item in the port (30.5% / 131 ms, docs/perf-method.md). It paints ONE SCAN LINE PER CHAIN, top down: $70/$71 = $6700 and $72/$73 = $6800, and $6700 - BBC_SCREEN_BASE ($5A80) = 3200 = 10*320 exactly, i.e. character row 10 / cell 0 / line 0 = DISPLAY LINE 80, while $6800 = $6700+256 is cell 32 of the same row. So the 40 chain units are the 40 CELLS ACROSS a line (unit i writes base + 8*i, and cells 32-39 come off the second pointer because 40*8 = 320 > 256), and X = $4F..$03 is the line, stepped by $7EF3 (+1 within a character row, +$139 across one). Confirmed independently on a real BBC: stores cover display lines 80..157, buckets 88..111 full at 320 = 8 lines x 40 cells (`make fbwrites`). Each unit is `LDY srcTable,X / BEQ / LDA #0 / STA srcTable,X / LDA $6000,Y / LDY #cell*8 / STA (zp),Y` over the $80-spaced source blocks $3000..$4380 — one block per CELL COLUMN, indexed by line — and A carries left to right, so a zero source means 'same byte as the cell to my LEFT'. THREE phases by how much of the line is painted: phase 1 ($7BE2, X=$4F..$2C) all 40 cells; phases 2 ($7D13, X=$2B..$1C) and 3 ($7F18, X=$1B..$03) plant an RTS to stop the chain at a per-line cell and compose the boundary byte themselves — the silhouette of the cockpit opening. Measured: 2093 units run per sweep for ~83 changed bytes (docs/direct-bitplane-plan.md §7a). Self-modifying by construction — 42 patch sites, docs/static-map.md §Open items 10.

view_paint_lines phase 2 (X=$2B..$1C): plants the chain-A stop RTS from $3150,X and the chain-B start from $30D0,X, runs the chain, then composes the two boundary bytes itself. Reached only by falling out of $7BE2.

view_paint_lines phase 3 (X=$1B..$03): as phase 2 but plants BOTH chains' stop cells ($3150,X and $3080,X) and both start offsets, and steps the scan-line pointers itself instead of via $7EF3. Reached only from $7D13; exits through view_paint_restore.

view_paint_lines' exit: puts `STA` ($91) back over the three RTS opcodes the sweep planted (the slots recorded in $7D24/$7F24/$7F7D) and `CPX` ($E0) back at $7EEE, leaving the chain unpatched for the next call.

[DERIVED] not a routine — the first of the two fully unrolled cell chains view_paint_lines runs, sixteen 17-byte units from $7C00 (cells 0-15 of the line), entered at a computed offset and terminated by a planted RTS. Its tail `JMP $7D56` makes chain B part of the same pass. Ghidra's function bracket here is an artefact of the computed JSR targets, not a body.
[DERIVED] the second unrolled cell chain, 24 units from $7D56 (cells 16-39, source blocks $3800..$4380). The last eight store through $72/$73 because the line's 320 bytes span two pages.

unit 10 of view_cell_chain_b, not a function start — it is a JSR target only because the computed call's fixed high operand byte is $7E. ⚠ Also the page whose low-byte patches reach the chain-B opcode slots: chain B's first ten slots ($7D65..$7DFE) are in page $7D, which no writer addresses, so they are plain stores.

[DERIVED] steps view_paint_lines' two destination pointers to the NEXT SCAN LINE — INC of $70/$72 inside a character row, +$139 (`CLC / ADC #$38` plus two `ADC #1`) to cross into the next one — then re-enters chain A at $7BF7, which loads the line's background byte from $38FC[$5F60,X and 3]. Never returns to its caller by falling out; only through a planted RTS in a chain.

⭐ THE DOUBLE-WIDTH ENTRY to vdu_char_def: stores the code at $62C3 then JMPs $509D, deliberately skipping $509B's `LDA #0 / STA $77` so the CALLER's $77 survives. $50AE then halves the glyph — bit 7 clear keeps its left four columns (AND #$F0), bit 7 set lifts its right four into place (ASL A x4) — and each half becomes one MODE 5 cell, so one glyph is drawn across two cells at double width. Measured on a real BBC: 4 entries at $509D from $508F, $77 in {$22,$FF}. Only caller: draw_gear_indicator.
